text: The unexamined life is not worth living.

text: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.
author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

text: Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
author: Lord Acton

text: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.

author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein

text: I think, therefore I am.
author: René Descartes

text: I have measured out my life with coffee spoons.
author: T. S. Eliot
work: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock

text: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: We all have strength enough to endure the misfortunes of others.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld

text: The heart has its reasons which reason knows nothing of.
author: Blaise Pascal

text: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
author: Japanese proverb

text: Still waters run deep.
author: English proverb

text: He who fights with monsters might take care lest he thereby become a monster. And when you gaze long into an abyss the abyss also gazes into you.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text:
I must not fear.
Fear is the mind-killer.
Fear is the little-death that brings total obliteration.
I will face my fear.
author: Frank Herbert

text: This is your life, and it's ending one minute at a time.
author: Chuck Palahniuk

text:
You can't remember your name?
No. But for some reason I remember yours.
author: Hayao Miyazaki

text: A heart is a heavy burden.
author: Hayao Miyazaki

text: The trouble with having an open mind, of course, is that people will insist on coming along and trying to put things in it.
author: Terry Pratchett

text: Light thinks it travels faster than anything but it is wrong. No matter how fast light travels it finds the darkness has always got there first, and is waiting for it.
author: Terry Pratchett

text: Gods don't like people not doing much work. People who aren't busy all the time might start to think.
author: Terry Pratchett

text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: Experience is the name everyone gives to their mistakes.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: Lay hold of today’s task, and you will not need to depend so much upon tomorrow’s. While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer.
author: Albert Camus

text: We are what we pretend to be, so we must be careful about what we pretend to be.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: I urge you to please notice when you are happy, and exclaim or murmur or think at some point, "If this isn't nice, I don't know what is."
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

text: Everything is an illusion in the mundane world. Only your conviction is real.
author: Shibumi
